strap: The day in one page · eight stories, six continents' worth of desks · every hour given in UTC

leads.head: Missile strike hits Zelensky's home city
leads.body: A Russian ballistic missile attack on the centre of President Volodymyr Zelensky's hometown killed two people and wounded 60, local officials said. Hours later he restated Ukraine's wish to join NATO.

leads.head: Army seizes 'El Chapo Isidro'
leads.body: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, on the FBI's ten-most-wanted list, was captured in a special-forces raid. Gunfights that followed across Sinaloa left at least 11 dead.
leads.src: The New York Times · CBC · FT

cards.head: Drone strike sets Russian cargo ship ablaze
cards.body: The Sparta II was hit in the eastern Baltic; Finland's PM said the war is 'spilling over' and tightened security.

cards.head: Eisenkot invites Likud to coalition talks
cards.body: The centrist Yashar leader asked Netanyahu's Likud to begin a 'marathon' of talks on Sunday.

cards.head: COP31 drags into overtime
cards.body: Talks overran as Saudi Arabia led opposition to naming a fossil-fuel phase-out; the EU raised the prospect of no deal.

cards.head: Funeral boat capsizes, killing 24
cards.body: A boat carrying mourners to a funeral went down in Bayelsa State; search teams kept looking for the missing.

cards.head: City votes for its Election Committee
cards.body: About 5,700 voters choose the 1,500-strong college that nominates candidates and picks the city's leader.

cards.head: Minister denies US report on AUKUS
cards.body: Australia's defence minister rejected a US press report on the submarine programme as 'wrong'.

briefs: FBI said to be investigating an apparent hack of its criminal database.
Burglars took a 'staggering' $22m from freight trains in carefully planned heists.
Quad, ASEAN-India and East Asia summits closed; India read out the takeaways.
India and Bulgaria discussed IMEC and the Black Sea situation.
US Central Command denied Iran's claim that a missile damaged an F-16.
Australia beat Wales 29-26 in the autumn internationals.
note: Headlines are the wires' own words, trimmed. Hours are each report's own timestamp, UTC.
